findings.text: follow-on: the commit adds one ruff finding on a changed path. At the reviewed head, `ruff check` over the five declared changed files reports four findings where the base revision of the same files reports three: the new one is PERF401 ("Use `list.extend` to create a transformed list") at promotion.py:8710, the `for payload in committed_review_payloads: committed_review_paths.append(...)` loop added by this commit. The repo's own rule is that a commit adds no findings on the paths it stages, and the reviewed manifest's evidence_inputs claims `ruff: check 7 findings on changed paths vs 10 at base (no added)` — the direction is right (no dimension of the change is a lint regression in spirit) but the conclusion is contradicted by measurement: the changed source paths gain exactly one. Small and non-blocking (the loop is the readable form here and the finding does not affect behaviour), but it should not be recorded as zero.

follow-on: list_plan_reviews(project=None) now calls flight.mounted_project_docs() inside its else branch, and that function fails closed (raises FlightConfigError) on malformed mounts.json. A listing that previously read only the staging root and always returned a list can now raise on a corrupt mounts file. This is probably intended (mount registration is the host's authority boundary and fail-closed is the module's documented contract), but it is a new failure surface on a read path, worth naming rather than leaving implicit; no test exercises the malformed-mounts case.

justifications.durability: Each of the four behaviours carries a named regression test and each is independently falsifiable: I mutated the reviewed head in a scratch copy (no .git) and the guarded test reddened every time with the expected id and EXIT=1 — return payloads[:1] (commit only the selected round) reddens test_promotion_commits_every_review_round_of_the_subject (1 failed, 5 passed); forcing the committed-tree branch to return without searching staging reddens test_stored_record_falls_through_to_staging_for_a_head_the_tree_lacks (1 failed); dropping the caller-supplied project reddens both project tests (2 failed); dropping the mount enumeration reddens both listing tests (2 failed). None of the failing ids appear in the head arm's 42 passed.
justifications.evidence: Independently reproduced rather than read: the reviewed head 15aaf3a40 re-run in its own clean worktree gives 42 passed EXIT=0 (review-head-gate.log, module.__file__ resolving to the reviewed worktree); the declared negative control reproduced by an independent mutation gives 1 failed, 5 passed, EXIT=1; three further mutations falsify the other three halves (review-negative-control-fallthrough/project/mounts.log). The one weakness is manifest accuracy, not the change: the ruff arm of evidence_inputs claims no added finding while the changed source paths gain a PERF401 at promotion.py:8710.
justifications.fit: Extends the owners the plan names rather than adding mechanisms: store_committed_review gains an optional project keyword, _commit_state_write already took a set of paths and now receives the record paths in the same landing set, list_plan_reviews adds mounted projects beside the staging directories, and stored_records_for_run reuses the store's own index (_store_index). Two fit concerns, both named as follow-ons: the added PERF401 finding against the repo's no-added-findings rule, and the new fail-closed failure surface on list_plan_reviews via mounted_project_docs.
justifications.goal_fidelity: All four brief gaps are implemented and load-bearing. Item 1: _delivered_review_payloads_for_commit now enumerates every stored round of the subject (delivered round plus every staging record for the resolved reviewed run id, deduplicated by review run id) and _complete_locked writes them all into the committed tree. Item 2: stored_record holds the committed selection and falls through to the staging store only when the committed tree carries records for the run but none at the named head. Item 3: store_committed_review resolves the project from the requesting caller when the record's body omits it, and stores it on the committed record. Item 4: list_plan_reviews enumerates flight.mounted_project_docs() beside the staging root. The four branch fixes rather than restate the plan.
justifications.reuse: Reuses review_module.committed_review_root, _select_stored_record, _store_index, _note_skipped_record, ledger_block, and promotion._restore_landing_writes; adds no new store path and no new mechanism. One new helper, stored_records_for_run, is justified: the existing by-head reader returns one record and the by-review-run lookup keys a different id, so committing every round needs the enumeration, and it is placed on the module that owns the store rather than inlined in promotion.
justifications.scope_discipline: Five files changed, all within the declared write paths: reckon/crew/review.py, reckon/crew/plan_review.py, reckon/crew/promotion.py, tests/test_bookkeeping_follows_the_run.py, tests/test_every_review_round_is_committed.py. Nothing outside the declaration is touched and no figure or fragment was written where the orientation file list named directories; recovery.py, which the brief explicitly leaves to a later node, is untouched.

raw_text: VERDICT goal: a promotion commits every stored review round of its subject, not only the round it selected for the promoted head, with three supporting repairs — the committed-tree reader falls through to staging at an uncommitted head, the committed store takes a record's project from the promoting run, and the plan-review listing enumerates mounted projects (reckon/crew/promotion.py:_delivered_review_payloads_for_commit, review.py:stored_record / store_committed_review / stored_records_for_run, plan_review.py:list_plan_reviews); all four reproduced by targeted mutation of the reviewed head. EVIDENCE: head gate independently re-run 42 passed EXIT=0 (module resolved to the reviewed worktree); four mutations red with the expected ids at EXIT=1 (every-round 1 failed; fall-through 1 failed; project 2 failed; mounts 2 failed); none of the failing ids appear in the head arm. SCOPE: five declared files, nothing else; no fragment or figure because the brief's done-when names no artifact. DURABILITY: each of the four behaviours has a named regression test and each is falsifiable. FIT: extends committed_review_root/store_committed_review/_commit_state_write and reuses the store index; TWO follow-ons — a new PERF401 finding at promotion.py:8710 against the repo's no-added-findings rule (contradicting the manifest's ruff claim), and a new fail-closed failure surface on list_plan_reviews via mounted_project_docs. REUSE: reuses _store_index, _select_stored_record, _restore_landing_writes and ledger_block; adds stored_records_for_run, justified. No blocking finding.
